metadata.title: Hospital Wing B - Progress Verification & Concrete Acceptance
metadata.sourceBrief: Investigate divergence between claimed contractor completion and verified site quality testing for Level 3 slab.
metadata.targetAudience: Project steering committee, main contractor commercial leads, and client representatives
metadata.intendedOutcome: Agree conditional progress certification tied strictly to cube 28-day core test results and remedial screed sign-off.

characters.name: Sarah Jenkins
characters.visualDescription: Professional site PPE, high-vis vest over formal attire, safety glasses resting on clipboard.
characters.communicationStyle: Structured, objective, demanding verified data before certifying payments.

characters.name: David Okafor
characters.visualDescription: Weathered site gear, hardhat, tablet showing QA inspection checklist.
characters.communicationStyle: Direct, safety-focused, grounded in British Standards and laboratory test logs.

characters.name: Marcus Vance
characters.visualDescription: High-vis vest over dark suit, holding interim valuation binder.
characters.communicationStyle: Assertive, focused on monthly billing milestones, cashflow preservation, and subcontractor liabilities.
constraints: Under pressure to meet Q3 valuation forecast

locations.name: Site Management Portakabin A
locations.description: Functional construction site meeting room with drawing boards, layout plans, and whiteboard showing progress curves.

locations.name: Level 3 Transfer Deck
locations.description: Exposed suspended concrete slab with test cores marked in yellow spray paint and curing blankets stacked.

evidence.claim: Cube test set C3-04 achieved only 28.5 MPa against the specified C35/45 structural strength at 7-day break.
Contractor valuation claims 58% cumulative completion for Level 3 slab, whereas verified certified progress stands at 42%.

turns.spokenText: Marcus, we cannot certify Application Nine as submitted. Your claimed fifty-eight percent progress on Level Three contradicts our physical QA sign-offs.
Sarah, the concrete is poured and cured. Our subcontractors have billed for one hundred and forty cubic metres, and withholding certification puts critical path trade cashflow at immediate risk.
We submitted 58% because the physical casting is complete. What justification exists for holding it down to 42%?
Because casting the deck is only the first criteria under clause six. A pour without conforming test certification is conditional placement, not accepted works.

screenInsert.title: Progress Verification Dashboard
screenInsert.description: Split bar chart showing 58% claimed vs 42% certified progress.

turns.spokenText: Here is the third-party lab certificate. Cube batch C3-04 broke at only 28.5 MPa on day seven against our design threshold of 35.0 MPa.
turns.onScreenText: LAB RECORD: 28.5 MPa (FAIL) vs 35.0 MPa SPECIFIED

turns.spokenText: That was an early break during unseasonable ground frost. Our structural consultant anticipates full strength recovery at twenty-eight days.
Anticipation does not satisfy Building Control. Until twenty-eight day cores demonstrate compliance, that structural bay remains under temporary propping restrictions.
Looking at Grid Line C on site, we also have significant surface cracking and uneven screed levels across bays four and five.
We can instruct the screed remedial crew tomorrow morning. If we rectify the finish, can we certify forty-two percent today?

production.bRollIntent: Cutaways of highlighted core drill markings and propped slab soffit.

turns.spokenText: We will certify 42% today, releasing 185000 GBP once the remedial defect notice is signed.
Agreed. I will issue the revised payment schedule before five PM.
Ensure your project teams enforce rigorous QA before filing valuations. Submit your verified inspection logs through the BuildTrack portal today.
turns.onScreenText: SUBMIT VERIFIED QA LOGS // BUILDTRACK PORTAL

onScreenInfo.title: Agreed Outcome
bulletPoints: Interim cert issued at 42% physical acceptance
